description: Learns a writer's voice from files they point it at (Markdown, PDF, Word; a file, folder or tag) and keeps what it learns in a separate store with profiles and slots per language and text type. Use when the user invokes Idiolect or /idiolect by name, asks to learn or add their voice from specific files or folders, asks about their voice profile, slots, confidence or store, asks to test their profile against a held-out text of their own, or asks to check, write or rewrite text with an explicit Idiolect profile, slot or store. Not for general requests such as "rewrite this in my voice" or "tighten this" without those.

results.query: /idiolect learn ~/Documents/Blog and pick up everything I published last year
Can you use Idiolect to learn my writing voice from the markdown files in my Obsidian vault, folder Writing/Newsletters? Do a dry run first so I can see what it would pick up.
What does my idiolect profile say about my sentence length? Which slots do I have by now and how confident is each one?

Check this LinkedIn post against my Idiolect profile before I publish it and tell me what's off: 'Most cloud cost overruns aren't technical. They're a meeting nobody scheduled. Here's the alert I set on every subscription now.'
Write a 300-word intro for this week's newsletter about Azure cost alerts with my idiolect profile, slot en.newsletter. Points: budgets are too late, alerts per resource group, one owner per alert.
I want to test my voice profile properly: hold out my post 'why I stopped using ARM templates', have it write a draft from a short brief and let me judge blind whether it reads like me.
rewrite the paragraph below with idiolect, depth=edit, profile jeff: 'In today's fast-paced world, leveraging automation is key to unlocking value across your organisation's cloud estate.'
Forget drafts/old-rant.md from my voice store, I co-wrote that one and it shouldn't count as my style.
Roll my idiolect profile back to the snapshot from before yesterday's learn, the new lessons it picked up are wrong.
Add these three Word documents to my voice profile so it learns from them: reports/q1-report.docx, reports/q2-report.docx and talks/keynote.docx
Rewrite this in my voice: 'We are pleased to announce that the new PowerShell module is now available on the gallery. It offers numerous improvements.'

Tighten this paragraph, it's too wordy: 'It is important to note that, in many cases, the configuration of the environment may, depending on circumstances, require additional steps that should be taken into account.'
Make this email to my client sound more professional but still warm: 'hey, the migration slipped a week, sorry, the vendor was late again.'
What is an idiolect in linguistics, and how does it differ from a dialect or a sociolect? Give a few examples.
Draft a friendly LinkedIn post announcing my new open-source PowerShell module for Azure landing zones, about 150 words.
Proofread this blog post for typos and grammar, keep my wording otherwise: 'Their are three ways to scope a Bicep deployment, and most teams only ever uses one.'
Create brand voice guidelines for my consultancy from our website copy and the last five proposals.
Summarise the notes I added to my Obsidian vault last week and list the open to-dos.
Here are two versions of my essay intro. Which one reads better and why? A: 'Nobody asked for another framework.' B: 'Frameworks multiply because nobody deletes one.'
Analyse the writing style of Hemingway's short stories and summarise the techniques he uses at sentence level.
